title: Why the Best Leaders Will Matter More, Not Less, in the AI Era
author: The Good Boss
summary: The author pushes back on the story that AI is shrinking the space for leaders. His central claim is that the anxiety rests on confusing management with leadership: management is visible work such as status updates and reporting that AI can absorb, while leadership is the less visible work of building trust and making hard calls with incomplete data. Drawing on the economic idea that value follows scarcity, he argues that judgment, trust and genuine connection become more valuable as management work becomes cheap. The leaders who should worry are those whose value was built only on the management layer. He closes with a reframe, asking what AI frees leaders to focus on rather than what it takes from them.
points: AI is absorbing the management layer (status updates, allocation, reporting) but is far from replacing leadership.
Because value follows scarcity, deeply human skills such as emotional intelligence and judgment under uncertainty rise in value as management work becomes abundant.
Judgment, trust and genuine connection are named as the capacities that matter more in an AI-saturated workplace.
Leaders whose identity rested on running process without building relationships are the ones genuinely exposed.
The practical reframe is to ask what AI frees you to focus on, not what it can now do that you used to do.
quotes: Most of the fear about AI and leadership comes from a single confusion: mistaking management for leadership.

Leadership is completely different. It’s the less visible work, such as building trust, making a hard call when the data is incomplete, and sitting with a team member in their worst week and making them feel like they still matter.

Strip away the management noise, and what’s left is the real leadership signal. And in a world flooded with AI-generated output, the leader who can offer genuine human judgment, presence, and trust becomes not just valuable, but essential.
AI can give you ten well-reasoned options, but it can’t tell you which one is right for your specific team, your specific culture, and your specific moment in time.
So, in a nutshell: AI isn’t replacing leadership. It’s exposing who was actually doing it in the first place.
Leadership was always the real job. Now, AI is just making it impossible to hide behind anything else.
